title: At TechBBQ, Europe’s AI conversations kept coming back to: Who’s actually in control?
slides: Who truly controls AI in Europe?
TechBBQ's loudest debate: open vs. closed AI.
The surprise: startups demand open-source, not regulation.
Your roadmap hinges on which model you choose now.
Decide before next quarter: pick your dependency.
thread_text:
1. Who really calls the shots?

At TechBBQ, startups shocked attendees by demanding open-source AI over regulation. The loudest debate revealed a power shift that could define your next move.

2. Open vs. closed: the clash

Closed models promise control but lock you in. Startups argue open-source fuels innovation and avoids vendor dependency. The choice isn't technical—it's strategic.

3. The surprise twist

Regulation wasn't the enemy. Founders fear missing out on AI's evolution more than legal risks. They want flexibility to pivot as models improve.

4. Your roadmap at stake

The model you pick now dictates your ability to adapt. Open-source allows swaps; closed ties you to upgrades. This decision affects every future AI feature.

5. Decide before next quarter

Test both on a real use case this week. Can you afford vendor lock-in? If not, start a pilot with an open model today.

instagram.caption:
Startups at TechBBQ told Europe's AI leaders they'd rather have open models than new laws.

The debate wasn't about safety vs. speed. Founders said closed systems like proprietary APIs lock them into one vendor's roadmap, while open models let them switch as tech improves. They fear missing the next breakthrough more than regulatory fines.

The model you choose this quarter decides whether your content pipeline can adapt next year — or stays hostage to someone else's upgrade schedule.

Test one open model on a real task this week and compare the output with what you use now. Which one actually gives you more control? 🧩

The decision isn't technical. It's dependency. ⚖️

What's your escape route? 🔄
